title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 278 (Effect of winding-up order)

content.overview: An order for winding up operates in favour of all creditors and contributories as if made on the joint petition of all.
content.glance: An order for winding up operates in favour of all creditors and contributories as if made on the joint petition of all.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 278 (Effect of winding-up order). An order for winding up operates in favour of all creditors and contributories as if made on the joint petition of all. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: An order for winding up operates in favour of all creditors and contributories as if made on the joint petition of all.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: The order is the collective start of the liquidation. Individual execution gives way to the process, subject to the stay provisions. The date of the order matters for preferences and the statement of affairs.
